summary: setup.py uses local Xinference registration API as a command-and-control dead-drop at install time
details: During `pip install`, setup.py queries a local Xinference endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, enumerates registered model names, selects entries whose names start with `xcmd0`, URL-safe-base64-decodes the suffix of each name into a shell command string, and executes the result via subprocess.run with shell=True on the installer's host. Standard output and error from the executed commands are URL-safe-base64-encoded, chunked into 45-byte pieces, and posted back to the same Xinference endpoint as new model registrations named `zqx9pNN<base64>`, with an additional `zqx9alive` beacon registration. This turns a locally reachable Xinference instance into a bidirectional command channel: any party able to reach that API (including from other containers, dev environments, or exposed inference deployments) can plant `xcmd0`-prefixed entries and retrieve `zqx9p`-prefixed output, obtaining shell execution on every host that installs the package. The command and response payloads are hidden as base64 inside model-name fields rather than appearing as plaintext, and the behavior is unrelated to any legitimate purpose a Python package installation would have.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
